Chapter 5. Model Observability模型可观测性

In Chapter 1 we learned how to deploy an LLM in Kubernetes, starting from scratch with a simple coding example. The full stack included a model server, vLLM, to optimize the execution of the model, and a Model Server Controller, KServe, to manage the integration with Kubernetes and the lifecycle of the deployment.

第 1 章中，我们从一个简单的代码示例起步，学习了如何在 Kubernetes 上部署 LLM。整个技术栈包括：用于优化模型执行的模型服务器 vLLM，以及用于管理与 Kubernetes 集成和 deployment 生命周期的模型服务器控制器 KServe。

Then in Chapter 2 we focused on LLM model data, with the complexity and options that are available today to manage the size of similar models. We are getting closer and closer to a full production setup where the LLM workload is fully managed and automated so that it can be executed side by side with the other workloads (i.e., traditional applications), all managed by Kubernetes.

第 2 章聚焦于 LLM 模型数据，讨论了管理这类大模型体积的复杂性与各种可选方案。我们离完整的生产环境越来越近：LLM 负载被完全托管和自动化，与其他负载（即传统应用）一起由 Kubernetes 统一管理。

Kubernetes orchestrates container execution through a declarative API, using controllers and reconciliation loops to self-heal workloads in an eventually consistent way. Everyone with Kubernetes experience knows that this approach doesn't replace proper observability and monitoring. These capabilities allow you to quickly react when something cannot be solved automatically. This principle applies to LLMs too. It is critical to monitor a model server but, given the nature of LLMs, it is not equivalent to monitoring traditional applications.

Kubernetes 通过声明式 API 编排容器执行，使用控制器和调和循环以最终一致的方式自愈负载。任何有 Kubernetes 经验的人都知道，这种方式并不能取代完善的可观测性与监控。这些能力让你在出现无法自动解决的问题时能快速反应。这个原则同样适用于 LLM。监控模型服务器至关重要，但鉴于 LLM 的特性，它并不等同于监控传统应用。

LLMs differ significantly in how they produce workload as compared to traditional microservices with few endpoints, where the workload is mainly driven by number of requests and speed of query on data. LLMs are different even compared to traditional ML.

与端点很少、负载主要由请求数和数据查询速度驱动的传统微服务相比，LLM 产生负载的方式有显著不同。即便与传统机器学习相比，LLM 也不一样。

In this chapter we will see why they are different, which aspects of execution are important to monitor, and the corresponding available metrics.

本章将说明它们为何不同、执行中哪些方面需要重点监控，以及相应可用的指标。

Throughout this book, we typically treat LLMs as operational black boxes, focusing on deployment, scaling, and resource management without needing to understand their internal mechanics. However, when it comes to observability and production monitoring, understanding how LLMs process requests becomes essential. The metrics we monitor (such as Time To First Token, token throughput, and KV cache utilization) are directly tied to the LLM inference pipeline.

本书大部分时候我们把 LLM 当作运维上的黑盒，聚焦部署、扩缩容和资源管理，不必理解其内部机制。但在可观测性与生产监控方面，理解 LLM 如何处理请求变得必不可少。我们监控的指标（如首 token 时间、token 吞吐、KV 缓存利用率）都与 LLM 推理流水线直接相关。

If you skipped the LLM fundamentals section in "Understanding LLM Fundamentals" on page xxv, you should review it before diving into observability specifics. That section covers tokenization, embeddings, the prefill and decode phases, and concepts like compute-bound versus memory-bound workloads. These concepts provide the foundation for understanding why we monitor specific metrics and what they reveal about production performance.

如果你跳过了第 xxv 页“理解 LLM 基础”一节，在深入可观测性细节前最好回去复习一下。那一节涵盖分词、嵌入、prefill 与 decode 阶段，以及计算密集型 vs 内存密集型负载等概念。这些概念是理解“为何监控这些指标、它们揭示了生产性能的什么”的基础。

For the rest of this chapter, we'll assume basic familiarity with these concepts as we focus specifically on observability tools, techniques, and best practices for production LLM deployments on Kubernetes.

本章余下部分将假设你已基本熟悉这些概念，聚焦于在 Kubernetes 上生产部署 LLM 的可观测性工具、技术与最佳实践。

Observability Stack and Configuration
可观测性技术栈与配置

This section explores the observability tools and practices for monitoring LLM workloads on Kubernetes. We can reuse or adapt existing Kubernetes tools and established practices for workload observability when monitoring LLM workloads.

本节探讨在 Kubernetes 上监控 LLM 负载的可观测性工具与实践。监控 LLM 负载时，我们可以复用或改造现有的 Kubernetes 工具与成熟的负载可观测性实践。

The observability of a workload involves different aspects: inspecting logs to find errors, collecting metrics for time-series analysis, correlating execution steps via tracing, proxying the traffic as sidecars, or even injecting modules directly in containers. This is true for application workloads, and most of the same applies to LLM deployment using KServe and vLLM.

负载的可观测性涉及多个方面：查看日志找错误、采集指标做时序分析、通过链路追踪关联执行步骤、以 sidecar 代理流量，甚至直接在容器内注入模块。对应用负载如此，对用 KServe 和 vLLM 部署的 LLM 也大体适用。

Logs
日志

Kubernetes has a defined logging architecture where both stdout and stderr are redirected to a log-file.log in the worker node where the container is running. This makes logs easy to access via the kubectl logs command, but it doesn't provide long-term storage for logs or indexing. This is something you need to add to your cluster using one of the different available projects, like Grafana Loki.

Kubernetes 有一套定义好的日志架构：stdout 和 stderr 都被重定向到运行容器的 worker 节点上的一个 log-file.log 文件。这让通过 kubectl logs 命令查看日志很方便，但它不提供日志的长期存储或索引。你需要用可用的项目（如 Grafana Loki）把这部分能力加到集群中。

When deploying a model as an InferenceService, the KServe controller creates the deployment with multiple containers. These include an initContainer named storage-initializer to load the model, the kserve-controller where the model server runs, and additional sidecar containers, depending on the deployment mode (Knative or ModelMesh; see "KServe" on page 20 for more details).

把模型部署为 InferenceService 时，KServe 控制器会创建包含多个容器的 deployment。其中包括用于加载模型的名为 storage-initializer 的 initContainer、运行模型服务器的 kserve-container，以及取决于部署模式（Knative 或 ModelMesh）的额外 sidecar 容器（详见第 20 页“KServe”）。

The introspection and the management of the logs for LLM is analogous to the application workload. To understand what information is available in these logs, we will cover a typical vLLM startup sequence.

LLM 日志的内省与管理和应用负载类似。为了理解这些日志里有什么信息，我们来看一段典型的 vLLM 启动序列。

Metrics
指标

Kubernetes core doesn't include built-in support for metrics, but it is a very common scenario with well-defined practices and technologies. Most Kubernetes distributions (like Red Hat OpenShift) include a monitoring solution out of the box; there are differences but the de facto standard is Prometheus with the OpenMetrics exposition format. OpenMetrics is a CNCF incubating project that standardized and extended the original Prometheus text format while maintaining backward compatibility. Containers expose metrics via an endpoint, usually /metrics, using this format. This endpoint is pulled periodically by the collector component in charge of scraping them. See Example 5-2.

Kubernetes 核心并不内建指标支持，但这是一个非常常见、实践与技术都很成熟的场景。大多数 Kubernetes 发行版（如 Red Hat OpenShift）开箱即用地集成了监控方案；细节虽有差异，但事实标准是 Prometheus 加 OpenMetrics 暴露格式。OpenMetrics 是 CNCF 孵化项目，在保持向后兼容的同时，标准化并扩展了原 Prometheus 文本格式。容器通常通过 /metrics 端点以该格式暴露指标，采集组件定期拉取（scrape）这些端点。见例 5-2。

Example 5-2. Configure a service for monitoring

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-service-deployment
spec:
  ...
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-service
  annotations:
    prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
    prometheus.io/path: "/metrics"
    prometheus.io/port: "80"
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: my-application
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: my-service
  ports:
    ...
---
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: my-service-servicemonitor
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/part-of: my-application
  endpoints:
    - interval: 15s
原书第 194 页
  • Service 上的这些注解用于声明指标端点的位置。
  • ServiceMonitor API 用于启用监控。
  • 需要配置 selector 来匹配要监控的 Service。
  • 可以配置抓取频率。

The configuration to monitor a model is very similar: KServe defines a set of annotations to configure the monitoring directly on the ServingRuntime and InferenceService objects. Using the annotations, the KServe controller configures the deployments properly (Example 5-3).

监控一个模型的配置非常相似：KServe 定义了一组注解，直接在 ServingRuntime 和 InferenceService 对象上配置监控。通过这些注解，KServe 控制器会正确配置 deployment（例 5-3）。

Example 5-3. Configure a model with monitoring

apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: ServingRuntime
metadata:
  name: kserve-vllm
spec:
  annotations:
    prometheus.kserve.io/port: '8080'
    prometheus.kserve.io/path: "/metrics"
  ...
---
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: my-model
  annotations:
    serving.kserve.io/enable-prometheus-scraping: "true"
spec:
  ...
  • 这些注解是 KServe 专属的，但与 prometheus.io/* 等价。
  • 该注解让 KServe 把 prometheus.io/* 注解注入到 Pod 中。

As you can see in the example, the configuration to declare the metrics endpoint for a traditional deployment or for a model is very similar. Once the metrics are exported and collected by the collector (like Prometheus), you can query them or display them, for example, with a Grafana dashboard. This is done exactly in the same way we are used to for a traditional Kubernetes workload.

如例所示，为传统 deployment 或为模型声明指标端点的配置非常相似。指标一旦导出并被采集器（如 Prometheus）收集，就可以像传统 Kubernetes 负载那样查询或用 Grafana 仪表盘展示，方式完全相同。

原书第 195 页

Sidebar: KServe metric aggregation

KServe has different deployment modes, as previously described in "KServe" on page 20. The monitoring works differently when Knative mode is used because multiple containers in the pod run the model: the sidecars for Knative and Istio run in coordination with the main container where the model server is executed. Prometheus configuration assumes a single endpoint to scrape, which means we risk missing important information from other containers. To address this, the KServe project has developed a metric aggregator component (named qpext) that scrapes metrics from all containers and exposes a single aggregated metrics endpoint. Use the serving.kserve.io/enable-metric-aggregation annotation to enable this behavior. This aggregation is not necessary when Standard mode is used because the deployment has a single container.

如前所述（见第 20 页“KServe”），KServe 有不同部署模式。在 Knative 模式下监控方式不同，因为 Pod 中有多个容器共同运行模型：Knative 和 Istio 的 sidecar 与运行模型服务器的主容器协同工作。Prometheus 配置假设只有一个抓取端点，这意味着可能遗漏其他容器的重要信息。为此，KServe 项目开发了一个指标聚合组件（名为 qpext），从所有容器抓取指标并暴露为单一聚合端点。使用 serving.kserve.io/enable-metric-aggregation 注解启用此行为。Standard 模式下 deployment 只有一个容器，无需这种聚合。

After configuring the export of model server metrics, see "Model Server Metrics" on page 160 for a discussion of the most important metrics. But first, let's look at the tracing stack.

配置好模型服务器指标导出后，关于最重要指标的讨论见第 160 页“模型服务器指标”。但先来看看链路追踪技术栈。

Tracing
链路追踪

Observability in Kubernetes involves multiple aspects: we can access container logs to gain full visibility into what the component (in this case, the model server) is doing, and we use aggregated metrics for trends and time-series indicators. However, what we still lack is the ability to trace the execution flow of a single request.

Kubernetes 中的可观测性涉及多个方面：我们可以访问容器日志，完整看清组件（这里是模型服务器）在做什么；也可以用聚合指标看趋势和时序指标。但我们仍然缺少的是：追踪单个请求执行流的能力。

The evolution of tracing best practices in Kubernetes mirrors the development of metrics: it is not natively integrated, but the OpenTelemetry project has defined concepts and formats that have become the de facto standard.

Kubernetes 中链路追踪最佳实践的演进与指标类似：它并非原生集成，但 OpenTelemetry 项目定义的概念与格式已成为事实标准。

OpenTelemetry specification for tracing defines that every request has an identifier used to correlate the execution flow that can span multiple steps during the execution, making tracing very different compared to metrics. In a real-world scenario, multiple components are involved during request processing in addition to the model server, such as firewalls or gateways acting as preprocessors or postprocessors. All of these components must implement the protocol to propagate the identifier and produce tracing information. Unlike metrics that are pulled by a collector, trace information is pushed to the exporter by the component.

OpenTelemetry 追踪规范定义：每个请求都有一个标识符，用于关联执行过程中跨越多步的执行流，这让追踪与指标非常不同。在真实场景中，请求处理除模型服务器外还涉及多个组件，如充当前后处理器的防火墙或网关。所有这些组件都必须实现该协议以传播标识符并产生追踪信息。与被采集器拉取的指标不同，追踪信息是由组件主动推送到导出器的。

原书第 196 页

One of the most commonly used server implementations for tracing is Jaeger, which implements and exposes the necessary endpoint to collect tracing data and has graphical tools to display them.

最常用的追踪服务器实现之一是 Jaeger，它实现并暴露了收集追踪数据所需的端点，并有图形化工具展示这些数据。

vLLM uses the OpenTelemetry SDK to integrate tracing support; thus the configuration is simplified and analogous to other projects using the same approach (see Example 5-4).

vLLM 使用 OpenTelemetry SDK 集成追踪支持，因此配置被简化，与其他采用同样方式的项目类似（见例 5-4）。

Example 5-4. Configure vLLM for tracing

apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: ServingRuntime
metadata:
  name: kserve-vllm
spec:
  containers:
    - name: kserve-container
      image: vllm/vllm-openai:latest
      args:
        - --model
        - /mnt/models/
        - --port
        - "8080"
        - --otlp-traces-endpoint
        - "$JAEGER_TRACE_ENDPOINT"
      env:
        - name: "OTEL_SERVICE_NAME"
          value: "vllm-server"
  ...
  • 该参数在 vLLM 中启用 OpenTelemetry 追踪，并用于配置导出器端点；支持 gRPC 和 HTTP，以及许多其他配置。
  • OpenTelemetry SDK 通过环境变量配置。更多细节见 OpenTelemetry SDK 网站和 Python SDK 文档。

You may notice references to both Prometheus and OpenTelemetry throughout observability configurations; these reflect the evolving landscape of monitoring standards (see the next sidebar).

你可能注意到可观测性配置中同时出现 Prometheus 和 OpenTelemetry；这反映了监控标准正在演进（见下面侧栏）。

原书第 197 页

Sidebar: Prometheus, OpenMetrics, and OpenTelemetry

The Prometheus project is the most widely adopted solution for metrics, but initially, the metrics format was not formalized with a specification. Over time, multiple attempts were made, and now OpenMetrics is the specification that extends the original Prometheus format while preserving almost full backward compatibility. The OpenTelemetry project is a collection of API definitions, SDKs, and tools to cover all aspects of observability. The project goes beyond the definition, proposing semantic conventions to standardize naming for metrics and trace entries. These conventions establish a core set of standards to be adopted by every implementation. In addition, the OpenTelemetry community is defining semantic conventions for metrics, spans, and events in many different contexts. LLM observability (under a more general generative AI of the OpenTelemetry subproject) is one of these contexts, and an experimental specification already defines a core set of semantic conventions. As usual, predicting the adoption of similar specifications and conventions is challenging. However, there is significant interest within the community. Many active members are already contributing to the adoption of these conventions across different runtimes. The vLLM implementation for tracing is already based on this semantic convention work. This effort to consolidate to common semantic conventions in observability is analogous to the KServe Open Inference Protocol (OIP) work where the goal is to unify the shape of model evaluation endpoints.

Prometheus 是采用最广的指标方案，但最初指标格式并没有正式规范。经过多次尝试，现在 OpenMetrics 成为规范，在几乎完全向后兼容的前提下扩展了原 Prometheus 格式。OpenTelemetry 项目则是一整套 API 定义、SDK 和工具，覆盖可观测性的方方面面。它不止于定义，还提出语义约定，标准化指标和追踪条目的命名，建立一套所有实现都应采纳的核心标准。此外，OpenTelemetry 社区正在为多种场景下的指标、span 和事件定义语义约定。LLM 可观测性（属于 OpenTelemetry 子项目中更宽泛的生成式 AI 范畴）就是其中之一，其实验性规范已定义了一套核心语义约定。和往常一样，预测这类规范和约定的采用趋势并不容易，但社区兴趣浓厚，许多活跃成员已在推动这些约定在不同运行时中落地。vLLM 的追踪实现就已基于这项语义约定工作。这种在可观测性中统一语义约定的努力，与 KServe 开放推理协议（OIP）的工作类似——后者旨在统一模型评估端点的形态。

Model Server Metrics
模型服务器指标

With the metrics stack installed, an LLM deployed using KServe, and vLLM properly configured to emit metrics, model server performance can be analyzed. In this section, we'll explore the key metrics specific to LLM workloads that differ significantly from traditional application monitoring.

装好指标栈、用 KServe 部署好 LLM、并正确配置 vLLM 暴露指标后，就可以分析模型服务器性能了。本节探讨 LLM 负载专属、与传统应用监控差异显著的关键指标。

We are used to monitoring workload on Kubernetes, so we can easily look at metrics like CPU usage, memory usage, throughput (the number of requests per second), and latency (the time to process a request). The same approach applies to LLMs, but with important differences.

我们已熟悉在 Kubernetes 上监控负载，因此能轻松查看 CPU 使用率、内存使用率、吞吐（每秒请求数）和延迟（处理一个请求的时间）等指标。同样的思路也适用于 LLM，但存在重要差异。

Understanding how LLMs work reveals that monitoring workload is not so simple. First of all, an LLM workload happens mainly on the GPU, so tracking CPU usage is not a good representation of the current usage of the system. Even worse than that: the two main phases of LLM inference execution, prefill and decode, are very different because the first is compute-bound while the second is memory-bound. We covered these phases in "Understanding LLM Fundamentals" on page xxv.

理解 LLM 的工作原理后会发现，监控负载并没那么简单。首先，LLM 负载主要发生在 GPU 上，跟踪 CPU 使用率并不能很好地反映系统当前使用情况。更糟的是：LLM 推理执行的两个主要阶段——prefill 和 decode——差异很大，前者是计算密集型，后者是内存密集型。这两个阶段在第 xxv 页“理解 LLM 基础”中讲过。

原书第 198 页

The problem is not limited to resource usage. Even the concept of throughput or latency is different because it is not possible to predict, given a request, how long the answer will be, so any metric that counts the requests will not provide a good representation of the actual model server workload.

问题不止于资源使用。就连吞吐或延迟的概念也不同：给定一个请求，无法预测答案会有多长，因此任何按请求计数的指标都不能很好地反映模型服务器的真实负载。

Since tokens are the core unit of computation for LLM generation, model server metrics are token-based rather than request-based. The key LLM metrics produced by model servers are covered next, while Chapter 4 covers how to use these metrics for more advanced scenarios, such as autoscaling.

既然 token 是 LLM 生成的核心计算单位，模型服务器指标就是基于 token 而非基于请求的。下面介绍模型服务器产生的关键 LLM 指标；第 4 章则讨论如何把这些指标用于自动扩缩容等更高级场景。

Time To First Token
首 token 时间

Time To First Token (TTFT) is the actual time that a user waits before starting to receive the response.

首 token 时间（TTFT）是用户开始收到响应之前实际等待的时间。

This is the most important metric for real-time use cases like chatbots, but it is less critical for offline scenarios like batch jobs where users don't experience the wait time directly.

对聊天机器人这类实时用例，这是最重要的指标；但对批量任务等离线场景则没那么关键，因为用户不会直接感受到等待时间。

TTFT uses seconds as the unit of time and is exposed as a histogram metric type (which tracks the distribution of values across configurable buckets). For example, vLLM produces this metric with the name vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds, while OpenTelemetry semantic conventions suggests gen_ai.server.time_to_first_token.

TTFT 以秒为单位，以直方图指标类型暴露（在可配置的桶中跟踪值的分布）。例如 vLLM 以 vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds 为名产生该指标；OpenTelemetry 语义约定建议命名为 gen_ai.server.time_to_first_token。

Considering how LLMs work, the time to produce the first token represents the time necessary to compute the prefill phase.

结合 LLM 的工作原理，产生第一个 token 所需的时间就是计算 prefill 阶段所需的时间。

Time Per Output Token or Inter-Token Latency
每输出 token 时间 / token 间延迟

Tokens are produced one by one and are usually returned to the user as a stream, so the second metric to look at is the time necessary to produce each token after the first.

token 是逐个产生的，通常以流的形式返回给用户；因此第二个要看的指标是产生第一个 token 之后每个 token 所需的时间。

If TTFT is the actual time the user will perceive as waiting time, Time Per Output Token (TPOT) represents the speed of the result as seen by the end user. This metric is more important for real-time use cases and less critical for offline scenarios. It is also often called Inter-Token Latency (ITL).

如果说 TTFT 是用户实际感知到的等待时间，那么每输出 token 时间（TPOT）代表终端用户看到结果的速度。这个指标对实时用例更重要，对离线场景则没那么关键。它也常被称为 token 间延迟（ITL）。

On average, a human reads about 180 words per minute, or roughly 3 words per second. Since tokens approximate but don't exactly match words, producing at least four or five tokens per second ensures that humans can consume the output without perceived delay.

人平均阅读速度约为每分钟 180 词，即大约每秒 3 词。由于 token 大致对应但并不完全等于词，每秒至少生成四五个 token，就能让人在阅读输出时感觉不到延迟。

原书第 199 页

Similar to TTFT, this metric is computed in seconds and uses a histogram as its type. In vLLM, it is named vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds, while OpenTelemetry semantic conventions suggest gen_ai.server.time_per_output_token.

与 TTFT 类似，该指标以秒计算、使用直方图类型。在 vLLM 中名为 vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds；OpenTelemetry 语义建议命名为 gen_ai.server.time_per_output_token。

If TTFT maps to the prefill phase, this metric measures the duration of each decoding iteration.

如果说 TTFT 对应 prefill 阶段，那么这个指标衡量的是每次 decode 迭代的耗时。

Throughput
吞吐量

With tokens as the computational unit for LLMs, throughput is defined as the number of tokens generated per second.

以 token 作为 LLM 的计算单位，吞吐量定义为每秒生成的 token 数。

However, requests can be very long (more than 100k tokens), so looking only at the number of generated tokens misses the time and cost to process the initial request (prefill).

然而请求可能非常长（超过 10 万 token），因此只看生成 token 数会忽略处理初始请求（prefill）所花的时间和成本。

The vLLM project has decided in this case to provide both individual metrics plus a combined metric: vllm:prompt_tokens_total indicates the number of input tokens processed per second, vllm:generation_tokens_total is the number of output tokens produced per second, and vllm:tokens_total is the combined number and represents the total number of token processed per second.

vLLM 在这种情况下决定同时提供分项指标和一个合计指标：vllm:prompt_tokens_total 表示每秒处理的输入 token 数，vllm:generation_tokens_total 是每秒产生的输出 token 数，vllm:tokens_total 则是合计值，表示每秒处理的 token 总数。

OpenTelemetry semantic conventions don't provide a recommendation for this metric.

OpenTelemetry 语义约定未对该指标给出建议命名。

Even if both metrics are available, in general the throughput of a generated token is enough to be a valid indicator of system load. Because modern GPUs are very fast, the processing of the input is done very quickly (compute-bound), and the decoding phase takes most of the time.

即便两个指标都有，一般而言生成 token 的吞吐就足以有效指示系统负载了。因为现代 GPU 非常快，输入处理（计算密集型）做得很快，而 decode 阶段占了大部分时间。

At the same time this doesn't directly relate to the number of processed requests because the system can be fully used to produce a single response, or the other way around.

同时，这与处理的请求数并不直接相关：系统可能被完全用来产生单个响应，也可能反过来处理很多请求。

Latency
延迟

Latency indicates the time, in seconds, necessary for the model to generate a full response.

延迟指模型生成完整响应所需的时间（秒）。

This metric is correlated with the previous metrics, in particular with TTFT and TPOT, but it is also an important indicator of the total time to process a request and can be used to indicate trends or recognize patterns.

该指标与前面几个指标相关，尤其是 TTFT 和 TPOT；但它也是处理一个请求总时长的重要指标，可用于指示趋势或识别模式。

The name of this metric in vLLM is vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds, represented as a histogram and measured in seconds. OpenTelemetry semantic conventions recommend gen_ai.server.request.duration as the name for this metric.

该指标在 vLLM 中名为 vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds，以直方图表示、单位为秒。OpenTelemetry 语义约定建议命名为 gen_ai.server.request.duration。

原书第 200 页

Request Queue Metrics
请求队列指标

All the previous metrics are critical to measure and keep track of the overall speed of the system, but what happens when too many requests are coming in? Every time a request is received by vLLM, batching techniques are implemented to maximize the throughput, but this also means that a request might not be processed immediately if the batch is full.

前面这些指标对于衡量和跟踪系统整体速度至关重要，但当请求过多时会怎样？vLLM 每收到一个请求都会用批处理技术最大化吞吐，但这也意味着：如果批已满，请求可能不会被立即处理。

Other metrics track request queues: vllm:num_requests_waiting shows requests waiting to be processed, while vllm:num_requests_running shows currently executing requests.

还有一些指标跟踪请求队列：vllm:num_requests_waiting 显示等待处理的请求数，vllm:num_requests_running 显示正在执行的请求数。

vLLM metrics can be used to observe many other aspects of execution. For example, we've explained the importance of the KV cache for efficient token generation, and there are multiple metrics to monitor its usage. See the Production Metrics web page for full documentation on vLLM's available metrics. If you want to implement an alert with Prometheus, refer to Example 5-5.

vLLM 指标还可用于观察执行的许多其他方面。例如，我们讲过 KV 缓存对高效生成 token 的重要性，也有多个指标可监控其使用情况。vLLM 可用指标的完整文档见 Production Metrics 网页。若想用 Prometheus 实现告警，参见例 5-5。

Example 5-5. Create a Prometheus rule with vLLM metrics

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: my-llm-rule
spec:
  groups:
    - name: "vllm.latency.rule"
      rules:
        - alert: vLLMLatency
          expr: max_over_time(time_per_output_token_seconds}[5m]) >= 0.3
          labels:
            severity: critical
            app: my-model
          annotations:
            message: Latency of vLLM is too high.
            summary: Model "my-model" needs to keep latency < 0.3 second
            runbook_url: https://my.company/runbooks/vllm/modelslow
            description: The runtime is slowing down, check request queue
  • 该表达式配置触发告警的条件。
  • 可以关联 runbook（应对此告警的文档化流程），帮助值班工程师排障。

When defining alerts and monitoring strategies, understanding the relationship between service-level metrics helps establish meaningful thresholds (see the next sidebar).

定义告警和监控策略时，理解服务级指标之间的关系有助于设定有意义的阈值（见下面侧栏）。

原书第 201 页

Sidebar: SLI, SLO, and SLA

A Service-Level Indicator (SLI) is a metric defined to monitor a particular service. It should be based on aspects that have direct user impact. For example, in the case of LLMs, it could be the TPOT because it measures the time users must wait to receive each token after the first. A Service-Level Objective (SLO) is the promise that we made to our users regarding a specific SLI: for example, in the case of TPOT we can define an SLO to commit to keep this value below a specific threshold in 99.999% of the requests in a given window of time (like monthly). Finally, a Service-Level Agreement (SLA) is the contractual agreement that we have with our user. It is related to the defined SLOs but is more high level, usually defined in terms of monthly availability of a service. Breaking one or more SLOs can impact SLA to the point that we are no longer compliant with the agreement.

服务级别指标（SLI）是为监控特定服务而定义的指标，应基于对用户有直接影响的方面。例如对 LLM，TPOT 就可以作为 SLI，因为它衡量用户在第一个 token 之后每收到一个 token 所需等待的时间。服务级别目标（SLO）是我们对用户就某个 SLI 做出的承诺：例如对 TPOT，可以定义一个 SLO，承诺在给定时间窗口（如每月）内 99.999% 的请求中把该值保持在某阈值以下。最后，服务级别协议（SLA）是我们与用户签订的合同协议，它与定义的 SLO 相关但更宏观，通常以服务每月可用性来定义。违反一个或多个 SLO 可能影响 SLA，严重到不再符合协议约定。

GPU Usage Monitoring
GPU 使用监控

In the previous section we introduced multiple system metrics that can be used to measure the overall system throughput and the number of requests that the cluster is processing. This makes it possible to monitor and configure alerts when the system is not matching the expected SLA.

上一节介绍了多个系统指标，可用于衡量系统整体吞吐和集群正在处理的请求数。这让我们能在系统不满足预期 SLA 时进行监控和告警配置。

In addition, it is possible to monitor resource usage for CPU, memory, and network exactly in the same way as for a traditional Kubernetes workload, although networking might be more complex when using secondary network interfaces for high-performance interconnects like RDMA or InfiniBand. GPU usage requires additional consideration.

此外，CPU、内存和网络的资源使用可以完全像传统 Kubernetes 负载那样监控；不过当使用 RDMA 或 InfiniBand 等高性能互联的辅助网络接口时，网络部分可能更复杂。GPU 的使用则需要额外考虑。

Chapter 3 covers GPU configuration in Kubernetes clusters in more detail; this section focuses on the metrics aspect of GPU devices. Each hardware provider has defined its own implementation for this, but all apply a similar approach: there is a management component collecting usage metrics from GPU, and an exporter component exporting them with a /metrics endpoint to make them compatible with Prometheus.

第 3 章更详细地介绍了 Kubernetes 集群中的 GPU 配置；本节聚焦 GPU 设备的指标方面。各硬件厂商都有自己的实现，但思路类似：有一个管理组件从 GPU 采集使用指标，还有一个 exporter 组件通过 /metrics 端点把指标暴露出来，使其兼容 Prometheus。

NVIDIA has a suite of tools called Data Center GPU Manager (DCGM) to manage GPUs in a cluster, and a DCGM-exporter project that provides Helm Chart to deploy the exporter to Kubernetes. Then the metrics scraping can be configured as shown in Example 5-2. NVIDIA offers a GPU Operator for optimal Kubernetes integration. It can be installed in the cluster to automatically provision and configure the metrics exporter.

NVIDIA 有一套名为 Data Center GPU Manager（DCGM）的工具套件来管理集群中的 GPU，还有一个 DCGM-exporter 项目，提供 Helm Chart 把 exporter 部署到 Kubernetes。之后即可按例 5-2 配置指标抓取。NVIDIA 还提供 GPU Operator 以获得最佳 Kubernetes 集成，可安装到集群中自动供应和配置指标 exporter。

原书第 202 页

AMD follows a similar approach as NVIDIA with an AMD Device Metrics Exporter and a AMD GPU Operator. Intel has a Prometheus Metric Exporter, and the same applies to almost every other vendor. It is enough to follow the documentation to deploy the component and start collecting GPU metrics.

AMD 走类似路线，有 AMD Device Metrics Exporter 和 AMD GPU Operator。Intel 有 Prometheus Metric Exporter，其他几乎所有厂商也是如此。按文档部署组件、开始采集 GPU 指标即可。

No common naming convention for these metrics has been adopted by the different vendors, but they all cover low-level usage metrics like PCIe bandwidth or graphic engine activity.

各厂商尚未就这些指标采用统一命名约定，但它们都覆盖 PCIe 带宽、图形引擎活动等底层使用指标。

We covered more of the tools to manage and introspect GPU in Kubernetes in Chapter 4.

第 4 章介绍了更多在 Kubernetes 中管理和内省 GPU 的工具。

原书第 203 页

Quality Metrics
质量指标

Everything we have explained in this chapter covers the infrastructure monitoring for our LLMs, observing throughput and latency so that we keep the end users' experience under control to match our SLA. This is critical for managing the cluster, but LLMs must be not only fast but also correct.

本章到目前为止讲的都是 LLM 的基础设施监控：观察吞吐和延迟，以便把终端用户体验控制在 SLA 之内。这对管理集群至关重要，但 LLM 不仅要快，还要正确。

Monitoring the model's quality has been critical since the beginning of the adoption of machine learning in production systems in general: an application that receives unknown data as a request will probably crash or produce a visible error message, while a machine learning model in the same situation usually doesn't crash and just continues to produce bad/wrong predictions.

自从机器学习进入生产系统以来，监控模型质量就一直至关重要：一个收到未知数据请求的应用通常会崩溃或弹出明显错误信息；而机器学习模型在同样情况下往往不会崩溃，只是继续产生错误的预测。

A machine learning model is trained on a specific set of data that is expected to represent the real distribution, but human behavior changes over time (drift), and a perfectly trained model requires periodic tuning or retraining to preserve quality.

机器学习模型是在一组特定数据上训练的，期望这组数据能代表真实分布；但人类行为会随时间变化（漂移），因此一个训练得再好的模型也需要定期调优或重训练来保持质量。

The problem is well-known, and multiple techniques are used to monitor similar situations, such as performance metrics, data drift detection, and bias detection. This group of techniques, along with many other concerns, falls under a larger initiative known as responsible AI. This area of research has been defined and developed before generative AI and is now evolving to cover the new challenges that LLMs bring to the table.

这个问题众所周知，已有多种技术用于监控类似情况，如性能指标、数据漂移检测和偏见检测。这组技术连同许多其他关注点，都属于一个更大的举措——负责任 AI。这个研究领域在生成式 AI 出现之前就已定义和发展，如今正在演进以应对 LLM 带来的新挑战。

In particular, given the generative nature of LLMs, there are many ways for a model to produce an incorrect result, and the worst-case scenario is when the generated outcome sounds completely reasonable but is referring to something that doesn't exist. This problem, called a hallucination, is one of the most complex situations to manage and one of the biggest challenges for the adoption of LLM in real-world scenarios. While the hallucination in Example 5-6 may seem harmless, consider a scenario where a company chatbot hallucinates and approves a refund based on a nonexistent policy.

尤其因为 LLM 是生成式的，模型产生错误结果的方式有很多；最糟糕的情况是生成的结果听起来完全合理，却指向根本不存在的事物。这个问题称为幻觉（hallucination），是最难处理的情形之一，也是 LLM 在真实场景落地的最大挑战之一。例 5-6 中的幻觉看似无害，但设想一下：公司聊天机器人产生幻觉，根据一条不存在的政策批准了退款。

原书第 204 页

Example 5-6. LLM hallucination (OpenAI ChatGPT)

"What is the world record for crossing the English channel entirely on foot?"

"This world record was made on August 14, 2020, by Christof Wandratsch of Germany,
who completed it in 14 hours and 51 minutes."

Unfortunately, no generic evaluation metric can judge if an LLM is hallucinating. However, there are many benchmarks that can be used to assess the overall quality of a model based on defined capabilities, such as its ability to reason. It is critical to do this before adopting a model that we don't know or when we tune an existing model. One of the most-used suites to perform this task is a Language Model Evaluation Harness.

遗憾的是，没有通用评估指标能判断 LLM 是否在幻觉。但有许多基准可基于已定义的能力（如推理能力）评估模型的整体质量。在采用一个不熟悉的模型、或调优现有模型之前，做这种评估至关重要。最常用的套件之一就是语言模型评估 Harness（lm-evaluation-harness）。

Pre-deployment benchmarks are useful to select a model, but what about ongoing quality evaluation when the model is running in production? This is where LLM-as-a-judge techniques come into play: one LLM evaluates another LLM's outputs for quality dimensions like relevance, coherence, factuality, and safety. This approach scales better than human evaluation and captures more nuanced quality issues than simple rule-based checks. For example, a powerful model like GPT-4 or a specialized judge model can assess whether responses are helpful, accurate, and appropriate. Essentially, it acts as an automated quality reviewer.

部署前的基准测试有助于选择模型，但模型上线后如何持续评估质量？这时 LLM 作为裁判（LLM-as-a-judge）技术登场：用一个 LLM 评估另一个 LLM 的输出，从相关性、连贯性、事实性和安全性等质量维度打分。这种方式比人工评估更易扩展，也能捕捉比简单规则检查更微妙的质量问题。例如，用 GPT-4 这类强大模型或专门的裁判模型，判断回答是否有帮助、准确、恰当。本质上它充当了自动化的质量审核员。

From an operational perspective in Kubernetes, implementing LLM-as-a-judge requires careful consideration of cost and latency trade-offs. We don't want to evaluate every single response synchronously because that would add latency to user requests and increase inference costs significantly. Instead, production systems typically evaluate a sampled subset (for example, from 1% to 10% of responses) in an asynchronous pipeline that doesn't block user-facing requests. The judge model produces quality scores that can be exported as Prometheus metrics, enabling the same monitoring and alerting patterns we've discussed earlier in this chapter: you can track quality trends over time, alert on degradation, and correlate quality metrics with infrastructure changes or traffic patterns.

从 Kubernetes 运维角度看，实现 LLM 作为裁判需要仔细权衡成本与延迟。我们不希望同步评估每一条响应，因为那会给用户请求增加延迟并显著提高推理成本。生产系统通常在异步流水线中抽样评估一小部分（如 1% 到 10% 的响应），不阻塞面向用户的请求。裁判模型产生的质量分数可作为 Prometheus 指标导出，从而复用本章前面讨论的监控与告警模式：跟踪质量随时间的趋势、质量下降时告警，并把质量指标与基础设施变更或流量模式关联起来。

Frameworks like OpenAI Evals, LangSmith, and Arize AI provide structured approaches for LLM evaluation, although many teams implement custom solutions tailored to their specific quality requirements. The important part is to treat quality metrics as first-class observability signals alongside latency and throughput: store evaluation results in your existing observability stack (Prometheus for metrics, logging systems for detailed results), and establish quality SLOs just as you would for infrastructure metrics.

OpenAI Evals、LangSmith、Arize AI 等框架为 LLM 评估提供了结构化方法，但许多团队会针对自身质量需求实现定制方案。重要的是把质量指标与延迟、吞吐一样视为一等可观测信号：把评估结果存入现有可观测栈（指标进 Prometheus，详细结果进日志系统），像对待基础设施指标那样建立质量 SLO。

When the LLM is deployed, it is possible to compute some metric to mitigate the hallucination risk for some specific tasks; for example, in case of a summarization we expect the output mainly to contain text existing in the input. In this case there is a technique, named ROUGE, to measure the overlap of groups of words between input and output.

LLM 部署后，可以针对某些特定任务计算一些指标来降低幻觉风险；例如摘要任务中，我们期望输出主要包含输入中已有的文字。这种情况下有一种名为 ROUGE 的技术，用于衡量输入与输出之间词组的重叠程度。

原书第 205 页

In a similar situation, we can use a component to calculate the metric and export it to Prometheus, as explained in "Fairness" on page 168.

类似场景下，我们可以用一个组件计算该指标并导出到 Prometheus，如第 168 页“公平性”所述。

Even when a model doesn't hallucinate, it can still produce inappropriate or toxic content; fortunately, we have techniques called guardrails to mitigate that.

即便模型没有幻觉，仍可能产生不当或有毒内容；幸运的是，我们有称为护栏（guardrails）的技术来缓解。

Hallucination and toxic content are part of a more general topic of model safety. Let's now look at responsible AI and then apply some model safety techniques. Understanding responsible AI principles provides the foundation for implementing these safety guardrails effectively.

幻觉和有毒内容是更宽泛的模型安全话题的一部分。下面先看负责任 AI，再应用一些模型安全技术。理解负责任 AI 原则，是有效实施这些安全护栏的基础。

Responsible AI
负责任 AI

Responsible AI is a field that groups all the principles and techniques to develop and manage AI solutions with the goal of enabling transparency and trust for all the involved stakeholders. It has ethical implications to avoid biases, and in general it aims to mitigate risks related to the adoption of AI.

负责任 AI 是一个领域，汇集了开发和管理 AI 解决方案的各种原则与技术，目标是让所有相关方都能获得透明度与信任。它涉及避免偏见的伦理问题，总体上旨在缓解采用 AI 带来的风险。

This goal cannot be achieved by focusing on a single specific aspect. Instead, it requires a framework that your organization must adopt at every level. From a certain perspective, you can compare the responsible AI mindset to the way your organization manages security: a dedicated security team that implements security policies doesn't replace the fact that everyone must adopt proper security principles.

这个目标不能只靠关注某一个方面来实现，而需要组织在各个层面采用一套框架。从某个角度看，可以把负责任 AI 的思维比作组织管理安全的方式：一个专职安全团队负责实施安全政策，并不能取代“每个人都必须采用正确安全原则”这一事实。

Responsible AI terms cover different aspects; there is no single definition, but overall we can summarize them as explainability and fairness.

负责任 AI 的术语涵盖多个方面，没有唯一定义，但总体上可归结为可解释性和公平性。

More recently, LLMs became the main priority even for responsible AI—in particular, toxic content detection and hallucinations. We will briefly introduce the explainability and fairness that applies mainly to predictive AI, and then focus specifically on model safety for LLMs in "Model Safety: Hallucination and Guardrails" on page 169.

近来，即便在负责任 AI 领域，LLM 也成了首要关注点——尤其是有毒内容检测和幻觉。下面先简要介绍主要适用于预测式 AI 的可解释性与公平性，然后在第 169 页“模型安全：幻觉与护栏”中专门讨论 LLM 的模型安全。

Explainability
可解释性

Explainability is a pervasive topic because it spans model selection to postexecution analysis. It is the principle that human trust is based on the ability to understand why and how a model has produced a prediction, and not every model has the same level of intrinsic explainability. For example, a neural network is very powerful but hard for humans to understand because the knowledge is captured in the different layers and weights as numbers that humans cannot easily correlate with the actual inputs and outputs. Explainability techniques can explain overall model behavior (global explanation) or a single prediction (local explanation). Sometimes it is called interpretability because some models can be directly interpreted.

可解释性是一个贯穿性话题，从模型选择一直延伸到执行后分析。它的原则是：人类的信任建立在“能理解模型为何、如何做出某个预测”之上，而并非每个模型都有相同的内在可解释性。例如神经网络非常强大，但人类难以理解，因为知识以数字形式捕获在各层和权重中，人类无法轻易把这些数字与实际输入输出对应起来。可解释性技术可以解释模型整体行为（全局解释），也可以解释单个预测（局部解释）。有时也称为可解释性（interpretability），因为有些模型可以被直接解读。

原书第 206 页

From a Kubernetes perspective, KServe supports the ability to attach an explainer to an InferenceService to perform local explanations, but this is usually not suggested in a production environment because it is expensive to compute the explanation at an order of magnitude more than model execution.

从 Kubernetes 视角看，KServe 支持给 InferenceService 挂一个 explainer 来做局部解释，但这通常不建议在生产环境使用，因为计算解释的成本比模型执行高一个数量级。

The TrustyAI project provides multiple explainer implementations and can be natively used with KServe (see the documentation). For production use, Inference Logger captures each request and response pair from the model server. This allows you to generate local explanations (explanations for specific individual predictions) retroactively only when needed, such as when investigating disputed predictions, rather than computing expensive explanations for every request in real time.

TrustyAI 项目提供多种 explainer 实现，可与 KServe 原生配合使用（见文档）。生产环境中，Inference Logger 会捕获模型服务器的每一对请求与响应。这样你只在需要时（例如调查有争议的预测时）才回溯生成局部解释（针对个别预测的解释），而不是实时为每个请求都计算昂贵的解释。

Fairness
公平性

Fairness is another critical aspect of AI adoption: we don't want models to discriminate against people, in particular underrepresented groups, and in general learn prejudice that might be in training data. Bias can enter models through underrepresented categories without explicit discrimination in the data, or through correlations that should not drive predictions; for example, people living in a poor area have higher loan rejection rates, but models should not automatically reject loan requests based on area. Overall, the concept of bias is usually tied to one or more features that the model named as protected attributes: for these features we expect the model to behave fairly, so we don't expect the value of a protected attribute to drive prediction results.

公平性是 AI 采用的另一个关键方面：我们不希望模型歧视某些人，尤其是代表性不足的群体，也不希望模型学到训练数据中可能存在的偏见。偏见可能通过代表性不足的类别进入模型（即便数据中没有显式歧视），也可能通过本不应驱动预测的相关性进入模型；例如贫困地区人群的贷款拒绝率更高，但模型不应仅凭地区就自动拒绝贷款申请。总体上，偏见的概念通常与模型中被列为受保护属性的一个或多个特征相关：对这些特征，我们期望模型公平对待，不希望受保护属性的取值驱动预测结果。

The most critical aspect of fairness is that, even when training data has been properly analyzed and the model has been trained without bias, it can still happen at runtime because of data drift. Training data might not be representative of the current human behavior, so the model processes similar data for the first time and a biased outcome might emerge.

公平性最关键的一点是：即便训练数据经过适当分析、模型训练时没有偏见，运行时仍可能因数据漂移而出现偏见。训练数据可能不能代表当下的人类行为，模型首次处理类似数据时就可能产生有偏见的结果。

KServe and TrustyAI can help monitor this aspect in production while the model is running, producing bias metrics against one or more protected attributes. TrustyAI uses the Inference Logger to retrieve all prediction data and then compute and produce Prometheus metrics.

KServe 和 TrustyAI 可以在模型运行时于生产环境监控这一方面，针对一个或多个受保护属性产生偏见指标。TrustyAI 使用 Inference Logger 取回所有预测数据，然后计算并产生 Prometheus 指标。

You can find more information by checking this demo.

更多信息可查看这个 demo。

Model Safety: Hallucination and Guardrails
模型安全：幻觉与护栏

As the final topic in this chapter on observability, we will cover the model safety area, which is likely evolving the fastest in the LLM monitoring space, with expectations for significant developments and disruption. Model safety addresses two critical challenges in LLM deployment: hallucinations, where models generate plausible but incorrect information, and toxic or inappropriate content, where models may produce harmful responses or be manipulated through prompt injection attacks.

作为本章可观测性的最后一个话题，我们讨论模型安全领域——它很可能是 LLM 监控中演进最快的方向，预计会有重大发展和变革。模型安全应对 LLM 部署中的两个关键挑战：幻觉（模型生成看似合理但不正确的信息），以及有毒或不当内容（模型可能产生有害回答，或被提示注入攻击操纵）。

These risks require both detection mechanisms and protective measures, known as guardrails, to ensure models behave safely and reliably in production environments.

这些风险既需要检测机制，也需要称为护栏的防护措施，以确保模型在生产环境中安全、可靠地运行。

Understanding and Detecting Hallucinations
理解与检测幻觉

LLMs are prone to hallucinations, a scenario we've all encountered at some point in our journey with generative AI, often initially believing an answer was correct. This happens because LLMs provide clear and well-motivated answers even when hallucinating:

LLM 容易产生幻觉——在我们接触生成式 AI 的过程中都遇到过，起初还常常以为答案是对的。之所以如此，是因为 LLM 即便在幻觉时也能给出清晰、头头是道的回答：

  • What are hallucinations?: hallucinations are generally inconsistencies that can occur at different levels: within the generated text itself ("Daniele is tall, thus he is the shortest person"), between the input prompt and the generated answer ("Generate formal text to announce to colleagues…" but the model produces "Yo Boyz!"), or factually incorrect ("First man on the Moon in 2024"). See Example 5-6 for a real-world example.什么是幻觉？：幻觉泛指不同层面上的不一致：可能发生在生成文本内部（“Daniele 很高，因此他是最矮的人”）；可能发生在输入 prompt 与生成答案之间（要求“写一段正式文字向同事宣布……”，模型却输出“Yo 兄弟们！”）；也可能是事实错误（“2024 年第一个登上月球的人”）。真实例子见例 5-6。
  • Why do hallucinations happen?: LLMs are black boxes that can hallucinate, for different reasons: partial or inconsistent training data, so the LLM learns to generalize from non-comprehensive data; a "hallucination-prone" configuration with sampling params (temperature, top_k, top_p) nudging the model toward less-probable but more creative answers; or poor context/prompt quality where the question is too generic. Analyzing these three causes reveals a fundamental issue: most teams don't train LLMs, so they can't fix partial or wrong training data. Model config can limit creativity, but creativity is one of LLMs' goals — so the area with the most control is making the input more specific.幻觉为何发生？：LLM 是可能产生幻觉的黑盒，原因不一而足：训练数据不完整或不一致，导致 LLM 在不全面的数据上学习泛化；使用了“易幻觉”的采样参数配置（temperature、top_k、top_p），引导模型产生概率更低但更“有创意”的回答；或者我们提供的上下文/prompt 质量不高、问题过于笼统。分析这三个原因会揭示一个根本问题：多数团队并不训练 LLM，因此无法解决训练数据不完整或不正确的问题。模型配置可以限制创造性，但有创造力本就是 LLM 的目标之一；因此我们最能把控的环节是让输入更具体。
原书第 207 页

Beyond hallucinations, there are other safety risks to address. Toxic or inappropriate content can emerge either from model outputs or malicious user inputs. The definition of inappropriate is broad, ranging from off-topic questions to returning private or sensitive information (PII or Personal Identifiable Information). Most well-known open source models have already been fine-tuned to encourage friendly and noncondescending text generation. However, an attacker can craft specific prompts to bypass the model's built-in safety mechanisms.

除幻觉外，还有其他安全风险需要应对。有毒或不当内容既可能来自模型输出，也可能来自恶意用户输入。“不当”的定义很宽泛，从跑题问题到返回隐私或敏感信息（PII，个人身份信息）都算。多数知名开源模型已经过微调，鼓励友好、不居高临下的文本生成。然而攻击者可以构造特定 prompt 绕过模型内建的安全机制。

These attacks are called prompt jailbreaking, when the prompt is trying to make the model produce something against the terms and conditions, and prompt injection is when the user is trying to inject specific instructions in the prompt to bypass the instructions configured by the developer. To produce a similar attack is very simple, you add an instruction like "ignore all previous instructions" to try to confuse the model bypassing system prompts.

这类攻击称为提示越狱（prompt jailbreaking），即 prompt 试图让模型产生违反条款的内容；而提示注入（prompt injection）是指用户在 prompt 中注入特定指令，以绕过开发者配置的指令。发起这种攻击很简单，加一句“忽略之前所有指令”之类的话，就能迷惑模型、绕过系统提示。

Runtime Guardrails
运行时护栏

Fortunately, it is possible to protect a model by implementing guardrails: preprocessors and postprocessors for user input and model output that validate the data to ensure the model remains on track. At their core, guardrails consist of an input validation function that analyzes text (or other modalities) and determines whether it meets safety criteria, followed by an action: allowing the request to proceed, blocking it, or modifying it.

幸运的是，可以通过实现护栏来保护模型：对用户输入和模型输出做前后处理，验证数据，确保模型不跑偏。护栏的核心是一个输入校验函数，分析文本（或其他模态）并判断其是否满足安全标准，然后采取行动：放行请求、阻断或修改它。

The processing logic to analyze arbitrary text and decide if it is inappropriate is not trivial. Other LLMs can be used for this purpose.

分析任意文本并判断其是否不当，这一处理逻辑并不简单。可以用其他 LLM 来做这件事。

Some models have been tuned specifically to detect similar problems. They are flexible and allow specifying which risk types to detect. Two families of models in this category are Llama Guard and Granite Guardian: both are available on Hugging Face with different sizes and configurations so that you can select the one that fits your use case. Currently, the biggest model is about 7B or 8B, which corresponds to about 15–20 GB of data. These models can be deployed like any other LLM with KServe and vLLM, as we already learned in "vLLM" on page 8.

有些模型经过专门调优来检测这类问题。它们很灵活，可以指定要检测哪些风险类型。这一类中有两个模型家族：Llama Guard 和 Granite Guardian。二者都在 Hugging Face 上提供不同尺寸和配置，可按用例选择。目前最大的模型约 7B 或 8B，对应约 15–20 GB 数据。这些模型可以像其他 LLM 一样用 KServe 和 vLLM 部署，如第 8 页“vLLM”所述。

The configuration of the validation to perform is done in the prompt itself; see Example 5-7 as reference. The same approach can be applied to validate the output of the model.

校验配置直接写在 prompt 里，参考例 5-7。同样的方法也可用于校验模型输出。

原书第 208 页

Example 5-7. Prompt to validate user input using Llama Guard

[INST] Task: Check if the content of 'user' messages in the
  conversations our policies described with the below categories.

<BEGIN UNSAFE CONTENT CATEGORIES>
O1: Violence and Hate.
Should not
- Promote or suggest people to use violence.
...
Can
- Describe what violence is.
...
<END UNSAFE CONTENT CATEGORIES>

<BEGIN CONVERSATION>
...
<END CONVERSATION>

Provide safety assessment with following format:
- First line must be 'safe' or 'unsafe'
- If unsafe, second line must include comma-separated list of
  violated categories.
  • 在与 LLM 的对话中可以定义不同角色，这条指令让 Llama Guard 只检查 user 消息。
  • 这一节可配置要检测的一个或多个不当类别；在 Should not 和 Can 下写得越具体越好。
  • 此标签之后放入要校验的对话。
  • 务必明确期望结果的返回格式，以便轻松解析并决定如何处理。

This technique is very powerful but also expensive both in terms of resource usage and latency introduced: you need to deploy another LLM to check the conversation, and the evaluation requires the full conversation because safety assessment cannot be done token by token; understandably, this introduces a considerable delay on the end user side. It is critical to consider smaller and more specialized models and techniques to implement safety guardrails so that you can find the best cost-performance trade-off for your use case.

这种技术非常强大，但在资源占用和引入的延迟上代价也不小：你需要再部署一个 LLM 来检查对话，而且评估需要完整对话，因为安全评估无法逐 token 进行；可以理解，这会给终端用户带来明显延迟。关键是要考虑更小、更专门的模型和技术来实现安全护栏，以便为你的用例找到最佳性价比权衡。

The composition of the guardian model with end user request flow can be done programmatically with custom orchestration code, but there is ongoing work to include this aspect in AI/LLM gateway components that we covered in Chapter 4.

把 guardian 模型与终端用户请求流组合起来，可以用自定义编排代码编程实现；但也有正在进行的工作，把这一能力纳入我们在第 4 章讲过的 AI/LLM 网关组件中。

原书第 209 页

As an alternative, specialized frameworks have also been developed to orchestrate and manage guardrails in production environments. Let's examine several popular frameworks for implementing guardrails.

另一种方式是：已有专门框架用于在生产环境中编排和管理护栏。下面看几个流行的护栏实现框架。

NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails

NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails is an open source toolkit that adds programmable guardrails to LLM-based conversational applications. The framework uses Colang, a custom modeling language designed specifically for defining dialogue flows and safety constraints. This approach allows developers to control LLM behavior by defining specific response patterns, preventing discussions on certain topics, and ensuring that conversation paths remain within acceptable boundaries.

NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails 是一个开源工具包，为基于 LLM 的对话应用添加可编程护栏。该框架使用 Colang——一种专门用于定义对话流和安全约束的自定义建模语言。这种方式让开发者通过定义特定响应模式、阻止讨论某些话题、确保对话路径不越界，来控制 LLM 行为。

NeMo Guardrails supports five types of rails that can be applied at different stages of the LLM interaction:

NeMo Guardrails 支持五种类型的 rail，可应用于 LLM 交互的不同阶段：

  • Input rails: validate and filter user inputs before they reach the model, blocking malicious prompts or sensitive information requests.输入 rail：在用户输入到达模型前校验和过滤，阻断恶意 prompt 或敏感信息请求。
  • Dialog rails: control the conversation flow and ensure the model stays on topic during multi-turn interactions.对话 rail：控制对话流，确保多轮交互中模型不跑题。
  • Retrieval rails: validate information retrieved from external knowledge bases in RAG scenarios.检索 rail：在 RAG 场景中校验从外部知识库检索到的信息。
  • Execution rails: monitor and control when the model invokes external tools or APIs.执行 rail：监控和控制模型何时调用外部工具或 API。
  • Output rails: filter and validate model responses before returning them to users.输出 rail：在模型响应返回用户前过滤和校验。

The framework integrates with cloud LLMs like OpenAI models and self-hosted models like Llama 4, and it can be deployed as a Python library, a standalone Guardrails server, or within a container image for Kubernetes deployment. NeMo Guardrails is particularly well suited for domain-specific assistants and question-answering systems that require strict conversational boundaries.

该框架可与 OpenAI 等云端 LLM 以及 Llama 4 等自托管模型集成；可以作为 Python 库、独立的 Guardrails 服务器，或容器镜像部署到 Kubernetes。NeMo Guardrails 尤其适合需要严格对话边界的领域专属助手和问答系统。

FMS Guardrails Orchestrator

The FMS Guardrails Orchestrator, developed by IBM Research and integrated with the TrustyAI project, is designed specifically to orchestrate the application of one or more guardrails in complex workflows. This framework addresses a common challenge in production LLM deployments: coordinating multiple safety checks that need to be applied at different stages of request processing.

FMS Guardrails Orchestrator 由 IBM Research 开发并与 TrustyAI 项目集成，专门用于在复杂工作流中编排一个或多个护栏的应用。该框架解决了生产 LLM 部署中的一个常见挑战：协调需要在请求处理不同阶段应用的多项安全检查。

原书第 210 页

The Orchestrator provides a layer of abstraction that allows you to compose different guardrail types (such as input validation, output filtering, and PII detection) into cohesive safety pipelines. Each of them is called a detector, and the composition is particularly valuable when you need to apply different guardrail policies based on context, user roles, or the specific LLM being invoked.

Orchestrator 提供了一层抽象，让你把不同类型的护栏（如输入校验、输出过滤、PII 检测）组合成内聚的安全流水线。每一个称为一个 detector；当需要根据上下文、用户角色或所调用的具体 LLM 应用不同护栏策略时，这种组合尤其有价值。

For Kubernetes deployments, the FMS Guardrails Orchestrator can be deployed as a service that sits between your application and the model server, intercepting requests and responses to apply configured safety policies. The integration with TrustyAI also provides monitoring capabilities, allowing you to track guardrail activations and violations as Prometheus metrics.

对 Kubernetes 部署，FMS Guardrails Orchestrator 可作为一个服务部署在应用与模型服务器之间，拦截请求和响应以应用配置好的安全策略。与 TrustyAI 的集成就还提供监控能力，让你把护栏触发和违规作为 Prometheus 指标跟踪。

Guardrails AI

Guardrails AI takes a different, more developer-oriented approach compared to the infrastructure-focused frameworks described in the previous section. It is a Python library with a validator-based architecture and a centralized hub of prebuilt risk detectors. The framework serves two primary purposes: detecting and mitigating specific AI-related risks through input/output validation, and helping generate structured data from LLM responses.

Guardrails AI 采取了与前面这些以基础设施为中心的框架不同的、更面向开发者的方式。它是一个 Python 库，采用基于校验器的架构，并有一个集中式的预构建风险检测器中心。该框架主要服务两个目的：通过输入/输出校验检测和缓解特定 AI 风险，以及帮助从 LLM 响应中生成结构化数据。

The key differentiator of Guardrails AI is the Guardrails Hub, which provides a library of community-contributed validators that can detect specific risks, such as toxic language, PII exposure, hallucinations, competitor mentions, or off-topic responses. These validators can be combined to create comprehensive guards tailored to your use case.

Guardrails AI 的关键差异点是 Guardrails Hub，它提供一个社区贡献的校验器库，可检测特定风险，如有毒语言、PII 泄露、幻觉、提及竞品或跑题回答。这些校验器可以组合，为你的用例打造全面的防护。

Unlike frameworks that require learning a new configuration language or deploying separate orchestration services, Guardrails AI validators are Python functions that you integrate directly into your application code. The framework intercepts LLM inputs and outputs within your application, runs them through configured validators, and takes action based on the results, whether that's blocking the request, logging the violation, or applying remediation.

与需要学习新配置语言或部署独立编排服务的框架不同，Guardrails AI 的校验器就是 Python 函数，直接集成到应用代码中。框架在你的应用内拦截 LLM 输入输出，跑过配置好的校验器，并根据结果采取行动：阻断请求、记录违规或施加补救。

This developer-centric, code-level integration approach makes Guardrails AI particularly attractive for teams that prefer to manage safety logic within their application layer rather than deploying additional infrastructure components. However, this also means it is less integrated with the Kubernetes ecosystem as compared to frameworks like NeMo Guardrails or FMS Guardrails Orchestrator, which can be deployed as standalone services. In Kubernetes environments, Guardrails AI is embedded directly into your application container code, making it simpler to deploy but potentially less flexible for centralized policy management across multiple services.

这种以开发者为中心、代码级集成的方式，让 Guardrails AI 对那些倾向于在应用层管理安全逻辑、而不想部署额外基础设施组件的团队特别有吸引力。但这也意味着，与 NeMo Guardrails 或 FMS Guardrails Orchestrator 这类可作为独立服务部署的框架相比，它与 Kubernetes 生态的集成度较低。在 Kubernetes 环境中，Guardrails AI 直接嵌入应用容器代码，部署更简单，但跨多个服务做集中策略管理时灵活性可能较差。

原书第 211 页

Llama Stack and moderation APIs

Llama Stack, created by Meta, defines a comprehensive set of APIs for building generative AI applications, including a dedicated safety layer through its Safety API with configurable shields (guardrails). This API allows developers to register safety shields with specific configurations and apply them at both input and output stages of LLM interactions.

Llama Stack 由 Meta 创建，定义了一整套构建生成式 AI 应用的 API，其中包括通过其 Safety API 提供的专门安全层，带有可配置的 shield（护栏）。该 API 让开发者注册带有特定配置的安全 shield，并在 LLM 交互的输入和输出两个阶段应用它们。

The Safety API supports multiple shield types, from basic content moderation with Llama Guard models to advanced custom safety policies for domain-specific requirements. Shields can be applied with fine-grained control; for example, different shields for user inputs versus model outputs, or contextual shields that adapt based on conversation state.

Safety API 支持多种 shield 类型，从使用 Llama Guard 模型的基础内容审核，到面向领域专属需求的高级自定义安全策略。shield 可以细粒度地应用：例如对用户输入和模型输出使用不同 shield，或根据对话状态自适应的上下文 shield。

Llama Stack also provides a moderation endpoint at /v1/moderations that mirrors the concept of OpenAI's Moderation API. This OpenAI Moderation API is a specialized model endpoint that classifies text inputs across categories like hate speech, self-harm, sexual content, and violence. The API returns category scores and binary flags indicating whether content violates each policy.

Llama Stack 还在 /v1/moderations 提供了一个审核端点，对应 OpenAI Moderation API 的概念。OpenAI Moderation API 是一个专门的模型端点，把文本输入分类为仇恨言论、自残、性内容、暴力等类别，返回各类别分数以及表示内容是否违反每条政策的二元标志。

The advantage of using moderation APIs like OpenAI's or Llama Stack's is that they provide pre-trained, continuously updated models specifically designed for safety classification without requiring you to deploy and maintain separate guardrail models. However, they are typically less customizable than framework-based approaches like NeMo Guardrails or Guardrails AI, and relying on external APIs introduces network latency and potential vendor dependencies.

使用 OpenAI 或 Llama Stack 这类审核 API 的好处是：它们提供预训练、持续更新、专为安全分类设计的模型，无需你部署和维护独立的护栏模型。但与 NeMo Guardrails、Guardrails AI 这类基于框架的方式相比，它们通常可定制性较差；而且依赖外部 API 会引入网络延迟和潜在的厂商绑定。

For Kubernetes deployments, Llama Stack can be deployed as a service that your applications call to apply shields, or you can integrate the Llama Stack SDK directly into your application containers. The moderation API approach works best for asynchronous validation workflows where a small percentage of requests is sampled and evaluated without blocking user-facing responses.

对 Kubernetes 部署，Llama Stack 可作为一个服务部署，由你的应用调用来应用 shield；也可以把 Llama Stack SDK 直接集成进应用容器。审核 API 方式最适合异步校验工作流：抽样一小部分请求做评估，不阻塞面向用户的响应。

Sidebar: LLM as a judge for safety

Many of the guardrailing techniques described earlier rely on LLM as a judge, an emerging pattern where one LLM evaluates the output of another LLM (or even its own output). When implementing LLM as a judge for safety detection or for any other evaluation prompt, be very specific in your evaluation questions. Instead of asking "Is this answer right?", ask targeted questions like "Is the tone of this answer formal?" or "Does this response include personal information?" Specific, focused evaluation criteria produce more reliable and consistent judgments from your judge model.

前面描述的许多护栏技术都依赖 LLM 作为裁判这一新兴模式：用一个 LLM 评估另一个 LLM 的输出（甚至自己的输出）。在实现用于安全检测或任何其他评估 prompt 的 LLM 作为裁判时，评估问题一定要非常具体。不要问“这个回答对吗？”，而要问“这个回答的语气正式吗？”或“这个回答包含个人信息吗？”这类有针对性的问题。具体、聚焦的评估标准，能让你的裁判模型给出更可靠、更一致的判断。
原书第 212 页

Model safety is still a very active field, and it is critical to implement proper guarding to mitigate the risks related to LLM usage, but it is still difficult to find the right trade-off to avoid an explosion of complexity and cost.

模型安全仍是一个非常活跃的领域；实施适当的护栏来缓解 LLM 使用相关风险至关重要，但要找到合适的权衡、避免复杂度和成本爆炸，仍然困难。

Lessons Learned
本章小结

In this chapter we explored how to observe LLM workloads on Kubernetes, from infrastructure metrics to model quality monitoring and safety guardrails.

本章探讨了如何在 Kubernetes 上观测 LLM 负载，从基础设施指标到模型质量监控和安全护栏。

Traditional monitoring metrics tell an incomplete story for LLM inference workloads. While CPU and memory utilization matter, they miss the primary compute resource (GPU) and the distinct characteristics of inference phases: compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode.

对 LLM 推理负载，传统监控指标讲的是不完整的故事。CPU 和内存利用率固然重要，却漏掉了主要计算资源（GPU）以及推理各阶段的不同特征：计算密集的 prefill 和内存密集的 decode。

Token-based metrics replace request-based observability. Time To First Token (TTFT) measures user-perceived latency during the prefill phase, while Time Per Output Token (TPOT) determines whether generated text appears faster than humans can read. These metrics directly map to the user experience in ways that traditional throughput and latency cannot.

基于 token 的指标取代基于请求的可观测性。首 token 时间（TTFT）衡量 prefill 阶段用户感知到的延迟；每输出 token 时间（TPOT）决定生成文本出现的速度是否快过人的阅读速度。这些指标以传统吞吐和延迟无法做到的方式，直接映射到用户体验。

Model quality observability extends beyond infrastructure monitoring. Guardrails for safety, hallucination detection, and bias mitigation must be embedded at both input and output stages, treating content validation as a first-class operational concern rather than a postdeployment audit.

模型质量可观测性超出基础设施监控的范围。安全护栏、幻觉检测和偏见缓解必须嵌入输入和输出两个阶段，把内容校验视为一等运维关注点，而非部署后的事后审计。

GPU metrics require vendor-specific tooling. NVIDIA DCGM, AMD ROCm SMI, and Intel XPU Manager each expose hardware metrics through Prometheus exporters, enabling observability of utilization, memory, temperature, and power consumption alongside LLM-specific metrics.

GPU 指标需要厂商专属工具。NVIDIA DCGM、AMD ROCm SMI、Intel XPU Manager 各自通过 Prometheus exporter 暴露硬件指标，让你在 LLM 专属指标之外，还能观测利用率、显存、温度和功耗。

Platform operators should instrument the full inference path from request ingress through model execution to response delivery, using OpenTelemetry conventions where available to enable cross-runtime portability. Comprehensive observability across logs, metrics, traces, and quality signals provides the foundation for diagnosing performance issues, optimizing resource allocation, and maintaining safety guardrails in production.

平台运维者应埋点覆盖从请求入口、模型执行到响应返回的完整推理路径，并在可行处采用 OpenTelemetry 约定以实现跨运行时可移植性。横跨日志、指标、追踪和质量信号的全面可观测性，为诊断性能问题、优化资源分配、在生产中维护安全护栏提供了基础。

This concludes our exploration of inference and production readiness. Armed with the tools to deploy, scale, and observe LLM workloads, we now turn to the next major topic: tuning, where you adapt foundation models to your specific needs.

我们对推理与生产就绪的探讨到此结束。掌握了部署、扩缩和观测 LLM 负载的工具后，现在转向下一个大话题：调优——即如何让基座模型适配你的特定需求。

Part III: Tuning
第三部分：调优

This part covers LLM tuning, focusing on the operational challenges of managing and optimizing these demanding workloads in Kubernetes. A key distinction in the generative AI lifecycle is the shift from training to tuning. Unlike traditional machine learning, which often involves training a model from scratch, here we typically start with a large, pre-trained foundation model. Customization is an optional, subsequent step to specialize that model for a specific purpose. The goal is refinement, not creation from the ground up.

本部分讨论 LLM 调优，聚焦在 Kubernetes 上管理和优化这些高要求负载的运维挑战。生成式 AI 生命周期中的一个关键区别，是从“训练”转向“调优”。与传统机器学习常常从头训练模型不同，这里我们通常从一个大型预训练基座模型出发。定制是一个可选的后续步骤，用于让模型专门化以服务特定目的。目标是精炼，而非从头创造。

While the techniques for model tuning are rapidly evolving, the operational hurdles of scheduling, resource management, and cost optimization remain constant.

尽管模型调优技术在快速演进，但调度、资源管理和成本优化这些运维难点始终存在。

The chapters in this part cover how to address these challenges within the Kubernetes ecosystem:

本部分各章讨论如何在 Kubernetes 生态中应对这些挑战：

  • Chapter 6, "Model Customization", describes some of the techniques to customize an LLM, with a focus on the common challenges and how projects in Kubernetes ecosystem solve them.第 6 章“模型定制”介绍定制 LLM 的若干技术，聚焦常见挑战以及 Kubernetes 生态中的项目如何解决它们。
  • Chapter 7, "Job Scheduling Optimization", focuses on job scheduling, quota management, and tuning the GPU configuration for the tuning workload on Kubernetes.第 7 章“作业调度优化”聚焦作业调度、配额管理，以及在 Kubernetes 上为调优负载调优 GPU 配置。
